entries.title: A Stronger Teacher Within: Strengthening MoE Models via On-Policy Bidirectional Distillation
summary: MoEvolve temporarily activates more experts, repairs their cooperation by distilling from the original model, strengthens the expanded model with verifiable-reward training, and distills its gains back into the original expert budget.

Across four tested mixture-of-experts backbones, this produces stronger domain-specific models without increasing their final activation budget, offering a way to improve a model using its own latent capacity instead of an external stronger teacher.

evidence.rationale: Pinned v1 Sections 3–6 and relevant Appendices A–I inspected, including restoration, RL, reverse distillation, domain-specific evaluation and wall-clock accounting. OLMoE-1B-7B, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, GPT-OSS-20B and Qwen3-30B-A3B are each trained as separate mathematics, code and ScienceQA checkpoints. Expansion uses up to all available experts, original-to-expanded reverse-KL OPD restores cooperation, SAPO unlocks capacity, and expanded-to-original ExOPD with reward scale 1.25 transfers it back. Tables 1–2 report up to 22.2 domain-average percentage points over the original and 6.5 over same-backbone RL; evaluations average ten samples per problem and three training seeds. The 8/16/32/48-hour per-domain budgets on 16 H20 GPUs include all MoEvolve phases and match the compared methods’ wall-clock allowances. Router/expert and transfer-objective ablations support the mechanism. The original LG October19 new-submission batch plus official Sunday20EDT schedule supports inferred first paper availability October19T00Z; original October16T09:23:22Z receipt is retained. Actual full-source discovery occurred during this delayed backfill run, not on the report date. No author code or trained-checkpoint release was verified.
evidence.limitations: This requires additional training, larger intermediate active compute, valid reward functions and token-probability access; it is not training-free or reward-free. Equal wall-clock time on this fixed hardware is not equal FLOPs or a universal cost comparison. Separate domain-specific checkpoints do not establish one model simultaneously improving all domains. Tested backbones are at most30B total parameters; this does not establish trillion-parameter scaling or robustness outside the selected tasks. Maximum-expert expansion, ExOPD and checkpoint selection are additional recipe choices. V2 received October20 is not used for this October19 record; no independent reproduction.

entries.title: Self-Evolving Coding Agents via Harness-Policy Optimization
summary: Self-HPO alternates failure-guided harness revisions with reinforcement learning of the coding policy, using the updated policy and its unsolved training tasks to guide the next search round.

With Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, average resolve rate across three SWE benchmarks rises from 57.8% to 64.8%, offering a practical recipe for improving the model and its execution scaffold together rather than optimizing either component in isolation.

evidence.rationale: Full Sections 2–3, Table 1–3 and relevant Appendices A–E inspected. Two rounds alternate six harness candidates with 50 GRPO/BAR updates on 2,484 Python engineering training tasks. The self-proposer sees training failures and reference fixes but must not inject reference patches into solving context. Main evaluation averages three runs on 500 SWE-Verified,300 SWE-Multilingual and642 public V2 SWE-Pro tasks. Self-HPO scores 69.5/59.7/65.2 versus 61.0/54.2/58.3 for Base and 67.5/56.3/61.8 for matched policy-only RLVR. Cross-combinations retain some gains separately, with the final pair 69.5 exceeding 64.5 from evolved harness/base policy and 64.4 from seed harness/final policy. Original cs.CL October 19 batch plus official Eastern announcement schedule supports inferred paper availability2026-10-19T00:00Z; October 16 receipt is preserved. GitHub initial content commitOctober 19 at 01:39Z and HF model sole initial-release commitOctober 19 at 01:41Z corroborate the same window; earlier empty destination creation dates do not establish an earlier method release.
evidence.limitations: Only one backbone and coding domain; harness and policy receive different optimization operations, so the comparison does not establish universal compute-normalized superiority. Training uses executable reference outcomes and proposer-accessible training fixes, and policy training required eight B200 GPUs. Three-run means do not prove general deployment reliability; no independent reproduction. External-proposer HPO 71.6 is a separate Opus 4.8 setting and is not attributed to Self-HPO.

entries.title: MS-Eval: Benchmarking Sub-Agent Delegation and Orchestration in MCP-Intensive Working Scenarios
summary: MS-Eval pairs 166 tool-intensive work tasks with annotated delegation plans and a controlled harness, evaluating when subagents help as well as their success, critical-path steps and API-token cost.

Its eight-model study shows that specialization and context offloading can help, while unnecessary delegation often adds cost; this gives agent builders a more informative comparison than assuming that adding subagents improves every model.

evidence.rationale: Full Sections 3–7, Table 1 and relevant Appendices A–D inspected. Tasks span eight Toolathlon-Gym scenarios, with 89 annotated as delegation-needed and 77 not-needed; four delegation variants share a Kimi-Code scaffold. A 166-task comparison evaluates eight models, while the variant comparison uses DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731. Specialized roles score MSQ 20.8 versus 11.6 for general roles and 17.6 for plan-first in that setup. Critical steps count each parallel wave by its slowest subagent, not measured wall time; API billing is a fixed-price estimate. The full-benchmark Kimi-K3 Spec result improves success 10.2 percentage points at 0.4 USD lower mean token cost per task, whereas tested closed models incur higher cost with lower success. Original cs.AI October 19 batch and official schedule support inferred paper availability2026-10-19T00:00Z, separate from October 16 receipt. The announced author repository was checked by HTML and API and returns 404; it is omitted from publication.links.
evidence.limitations: One simulated tool environment and one harness; role prompts change the main agent even when it delegates nothing, and 305 of 625 categorized beneficial cases are main-agent-only. Delegation priors reflect the authors' parallelism/context-offloading assumptions; matching uses an LLM tagger and the custom MSQ weighting is not a universal quality score. Resource utilities condition on selected/successful subsets, and efficiency is critical steps rather than latency. No author implementation or independent reproduction verified.

entries.title: BaGuaLu-2: Taming Dynamic Memory Fluctuation for Efficient MoE Model Training over 10,000 GPUs
summary: BaGuaLu-2 adjusts activation-memory budgets for each pipeline microbatch and combines recomputation, offloading and reduced-precision storage when mixture-of-experts routing creates temporary load spikes.
Its detailed paper explains how a cost model and interleaved execution of neighboring batches can absorb those spikes without restarting training, improving utilization of large training clusters.

evidence.rationale: Read full SectionsI-VIII, Algorithms1-2 and evaluationVI, including the dependency conditions of fused dual-batch scheduling. Per-operator time/memory curves guide pipeline-phase budgets and a greedy conflict-checked mitigation selector; a compacted/cached dynamic program overlaps forward, backward, prior-batch offload and next-batch recovery. All evaluated pipeline degrees are at least4. On128-12,288 unnamed vendor GPUs (480TFLOP/s BF16,64GB HBM each;8/node,400GB/s intranode,4x400Gb/s internode), authors report mean throughput gains1.14x over Megatron-Kuai and1.13x over AdaPipe, with2.012EFLOP/s and about35%MFU for a1040B-parameter MoE at12,288GPUs. Baselines use the same initial parallelism and are adapted from dense-model systems. Paper receipt October16 07:40:24Z is preserved; the new full paper is in the original cs.DC Monday19 batch, whose release is inferred as October19T00Z from the official Sunday20Eastern schedule. The prior SC26 program already carried the broad mechanism and headline numbers; this entry selects the new inspectable full analysis, algorithms, configuration accounting and ablations, not a first announcement of those claims.
evidence.limitations: Throughput includes baseline OOM/restart warmup overhead but excludes human diagnosis time; it is not a restart-free kernel-speed comparison. Baselines are modified: only AdaPipe recomputation is enabled, and Megatron-Kuai receives MoE memory terms. The fused scheduling independence argument requires pipeline degree greater than2 and corresponding barriers; it is not a generic arbitrary-pipeline guarantee. Model configurations are GLM-derived and hardware-co-designed, not unmodified public checkpoints. Quantized activation storage is one allowed mitigation; no long-run convergence/quality study or public BaGuaLu-2 implementation was verified. Hardware vendor is not identified and no independent reproduction was performed.
